statement: If K is a compact metric space and W>0, the finite positive Borel measures on K with total mass at most W form a compact metric space under the bounded-Lipschitz metric.

quantifiers.measures: all finite positive Borel measures mu with mu(K)<=W
quantifiers.compactness: every sequence has a d_BL-convergent subsequence with limit in the same set

proof_obligations: d_BL is a separating metric on the bounded-mass positive measures.
The d_BL topology equals weak convergence on this set.
The family is uniformly tight and weakly sequentially compact.
Every weak subsequential limit remains positive with mass at most W.
verification_condition: A machine-checked dependency certificate covers every obligation, a complete symbolic derivation audits the classical theorem applications, an independent SMT checker validates the algebraic contradiction steps, and the noncompact-domain delta sequence is rejected.
